title: Rational-point criterion for faithful flatness of affine group homomorphisms
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Group schemes and homomorphisms are as in [def-sc-group-scheme], smoothness as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and finite type as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $H_1,H_2$ be affine $F$-group schemes of finite type, with $H_2$ smooth, and let $f:H_1\to H_2$ be a homomorphism. Then $f$ is faithfully flat if and only if the group homomorphism $f:H_1(F)\to H_2(F)$ is surjective. Faithfully flat means that the induced map of coordinate algebras makes the target algebra a faithfully flat module: extension of scalars is exact and detects zero modules.

source.place: Proposition 5.47, printed p.110 (with Theorem 5.39 for the image used in its proof)

proof.text: Put $A=F[H_2]$, $B=F[H_1]$, and let $\alpha:A\to B$ be induced by $f$. Assume $\alpha$ faithfully flat. A point $y\in H_2(F)$ gives $y^*:A\to F$ with maximal kernel $\mathfrak m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum], some prime $\mathfrak p\subset B$ contracts to $\mathfrak m$. Choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak n\supseteq\mathfrak p$. Its contraction is proper and contains $\mathfrak m$, hence equals $\mathfrak m$. By clause (1) of [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing], $B/\mathfrak n=F$ as an $F$-algebra. The resulting $x^*:B\to F$ satisfies $x^*\alpha=y^*$: both factor through $A/\mathfrak m=F$ and are $F$-algebra maps. Thus $f(x)=y$. No smoothness of $H_1$ or $H_2$ was used in this direction.

source.place: Proposition 5.47, printed p.110; affine image factorization Theorem 3.34, printed p.75

proof.text: Conversely assume $f:H_1(F)\to H_2(F)$ surjective. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-homomorphism-flat-image] to write $f=j\circ q$ (its $u$ is written $q$ here) with $q:H_1\to I$ faithfully flat on coordinate algebras and $j:I\hookrightarrow H_2$ a closed immersion. Both groups are affine of finite type, exactly the hypotheses of that node; it permits a nonreduced source. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], write $I=\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ for an ideal $J\subset A$. Every $y\in H_2(F)$ equals $j(q(x))$ for some $x\in H_1(F)$, so $y^*(a)=0$ for every $a\in J$.

source.place: Proposition 5.47, printed p.110; affine image factorization Theorem 3.34, printed p.75

proof.text: The structure morphism of $H_2$ is smooth. By [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] its fibre over the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}F$, namely $H_2$, is geometrically reduced, hence reduced. By [def-pc-reduced-scheme] its global coordinate ring $A$ is reduced. Clause (2) of [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing] now gives $a=0$ for every $a\in J$, since step 2 showed vanishing at all $F$-points. Thus $J=0$. The coordinate map $A\to A/J$ is an isomorphism, and $\alpha$ identifies with the faithfully flat coordinate map of $q$. Hence $f$ is faithfully flat, completing the equivalence.
